section_entries.label: 5. Other Lehmer pairs
section_entries.mathematical_role: Uses record-small gaps to choose a higher pair, certifies it by local summation plus two tail bounds, and obtains the sharper lower bound.

unit_result_entry.title: Record-small consecutive gaps prioritize candidate Lehmer pairs
unit_result_entry.why_material: Among record-setting consecutive zero gaps, early entries need not satisfy the stronger Lehmer condition, but the dominance of the squared-gap term makes the smallest available gap a rational candidate for the best lower bound. This distinguishes candidate retrieval from certification.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Defines the record-gap list, notes that close pairs are not automatically Lehmer pairs, selects the final pair, and records the precision and provenance of the zeros.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Moderate numerical dependence. The selection principle is clear, while the exact indices, gap, and claimed decimal accuracy should be verified against the scan and underlying data.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The pair-derived bound is dominated by the squared gap
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Order-of-magnitude changes to the upper estimate for the environmental term barely affect the first significant digits of the threshold bound. A series expansion explains this stability: the leading contribution depends on minus one eighth of the squared gap.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A high-index pair is certified by a local window plus two tail controls
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The environmental sum for the selected high pair is partitioned into 5,000 nearby zeros on each side, a finite remote block, and the far tail. Crude but explicit bounds on both omitted regions suffice to establish the strict Lehmer inequality.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Record-small gaps efficiently rank candidates because the pair-derived bound is led by the squared gap, but only an environmental-sum certificate upgrades a candidate to a Lehmer pair.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The heuristic is demonstrated on two familiar numerical cases and is not evidence that every record gap qualifies.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Candidate retrieval by tiny gaps is distinct from Lehmer certification

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Each Lehmer pair supplies a negative lower bound, and an infinite sequence of certified gaps shrinking to zero would make those bounds approach zero, forcing the threshold to be nonnegative while remaining compatible with the Riemann Hypothesis at equality.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source does not prove the existence of infinitely many Lehmer pairs; its conclusion is explicitly predictive.
